title: A profile name is its filename stem by enforced invariant, and PROFILE_NAME admits every Windows reserved device name, so lore accepts a profile whose committed file cannot exist on Windows
description:
Measured in answer to a bounded question from opum-agent: does any existing name -- profile name,
workspaceId, memberId, linkId -- become a filesystem path segment on any platform? Answer: NO for three of
the four, YES for the profile name. Measured against origin/dev a94bf095. The REMEDY IS NOT DECIDED HERE:
opum-agent ruled that ruling 11 (ADR-0021 Amendment 4, mandatory hyphen) governs the citation name only and
does not reach existing surfaces, and that a YES here returns to it as its own decision with its own
compatibility analysis. Filed so the measurement is answerable from a record.

THE THREE THAT ARE NOT PATH SEGMENTS -- searched src/ for join()/resolve() taking any of them, and for any
interpolation of them into a path; no hits of either kind.
 - workspaceId: hashed (src/core/workspace-contract.ts:173, digest("lore-workspace/1\0" + workspaceId)) or
   used in messages. Never a path.
 - memberId: a member's root comes from an explicit `locator` in the manifest, never from the id --
   resolveMemberRoot (src/core/workspace-source.ts:204-205) does
   `isAbsolute(locator) ? resolve(locator) : resolve(dirname(manifestPath), locator)`. memberId otherwise
   appears only in messages, digests, and composite keys ("${memberId}::${sourceId}" at :212,
   "${memberId}\0${value}" at workspace-projection.ts:385).
 - linkId: messages, uniqueness assertions, a digest (workspace-contract.ts:337), and as
   workspaceSourceRecordKey (workspace-projection.ts:188) -- a record key, not a path.

THE ONE THAT IS. A profile name is its own filename stem, BY ENFORCED INVARIANT, not by convention:
 - loadAgentProfiles enumerates .lore/agents/*.toml and derives `stem` from the filename
   (src/core/agent-profile.ts:81, `entry.name.slice(0, -".toml".length)`).
 - compileProfile throws unless the declared name equals that stem: `if (file.name !== stem)` ...
   "declares name X but its filename stem is Y" / "make the profile name and filename stem identical".
 - PROFILE_NAME is /^[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$/ (:45). It permits UNBROKEN alphanumerics, so `con`, `prn`,
   `aux`, `nul`, `com1`-`com9` and `lpt1`-`lpt9` all validate.
So the name and the path segment are the same string, and the validator accepts the whole Windows reserved
device-name class.

DIRECTION, STATED PRECISELY BECAUSE IT CHANGES THE SEVERITY. lore never CONSTRUCTS the read path from a
user-supplied name -- it enumerates the directory and validates the declared name against what it found.
But two error paths instruct the user to create the file: agent-profile.ts:146
`add ${AGENT_PROFILES_DIR}/${name}.toml or run \`lore agent list\`` for a missing profile, and :409 the same
for a missing delegate. So lore will tell a user to create `.lore/agents/con.toml`.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN A LOCAL INCONVENIENCE: .lore/agents/ IS COMMITTED (git ls-files .lore/agents/ ->
implementation.toml, review.toml, verification.toml, and .gitignore's note says .lore/agents/ is
deliberately not ignored). A profile named with a reserved device name therefore produces a committed file
that cannot be checked out on Windows at all -- a portability defect in shared content, not just a local
one, and lore's own validator would accept the name that creates it.

MEASURED VS INFERRED, kept separate on purpose. Measured here: the enforced name-equals-stem invariant, the
regex and what it admits, the two remediation messages, and that .lore/agents/ is tracked. INFERRED, not
measured on Windows: that `con.toml` is unusable there. That rests on the extension-independence the ADR
records from primary source ("NUL.txt and NUL.tar.gz are both equivalent to NUL", cited in OPAG-212). No
Windows measurement was taken and none is claimed.

NOT CURRENTLY TRIGGERED: the three committed profiles are `implementation`, `review` and `verification`,
none reserved. This is latent, not live-breaking. Worth noting for whoever weighs a remedy: all three are
UNBROKEN single words, so this surface's own convention is the shape ruling 11 would forbid -- which is
independent evidence for opum-agent's decision not to extend ruling 11 here, and a reason a mandatory-hyphen
remedy would be expensive on this surface specifically.
